item.title: Simbu secures record STEM scholarship intake for studies abroad
item.description: 14 high-achieving Grade 12 students from Simbu Province have been selected to pursue overseas tertiary studies under the national Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics [STEM] scholarship program. The cohort is part of a total 137 students selected nationwide for the 2026 program, marking one of Simbu's largest intakes to date under the government initiative.
item.content:encoded:
14 high-achieving Grade 12 students from Simbu Province have been selected to pursue overseas tertiary studies under the national Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics [STEM] scholarship program.

The cohort is part of a total 137 students selected nationwide for the 2026 program, marking one of Simbu's largest intakes to date under the government initiative.

The selected students completed their specialized STEM curriculum across Papua New Guinea's six designated National Schools of Excellence in Aiyura [Eastern Highlands], Sogeri [Central], Port Moresby [NCD], Wawin [Morobe], Kerevat [East New Britain], and Passam [East Sepik].

STEM curriculum developer Dr Clement Waine commended the achievements, stating that the results reflect a growing academic standard in the province.

"We have finally lifted Simbu's numbers. This is a proud moment," Dr Waine said. "I encourage our students to uphold the standard and make the province proud."

The national STEM program aims to strengthen Papua New Guinea's technical workforce by placing top secondary graduates in reputable universities in the United States to complete degrees in science and technology fields.

Local education stakeholders and provincial leaders have welcomed the announcement, urging the incoming scholars to return upon completion of their studies to contribute to national development in health, infrastructure, and technology sectors.

item.content:encoded:
A new tour operator in Milne Bay province is extending an invite to Papua New Guineans who wish to join a two-day tour in Japan scheduled for June, 2027. ‎ ‎Takita Travel and Tours is calling on interested tour operators, sight owners, groups and individuals to register as invitation for the adventure, which closes on Sunday, August 16 2026. ‎ ‎With over 25 years of working experience in the Tourism and Hospitality industry, owner and tour Guide for Takita Travel and Tours, Gali Joel, said Papua New Guineans need to be exposed overseas to experience the diverse opportunities and activities the tourism industry offers. ‎ ‎"We'd like to have an experience where we can also impart to our tourists when we bring them to our tour sites" she said.

"So when customers come to our sites, they will want to experience something so for us we are going to Japan to see developments that we don't have in our country" ‎ ‎Joel said this will be the first international trip organized by Takita Travel and Tours, adding that with Gurney International Airport opening next week, it will be a bonus. ‎ ‎"I worked 17 years with Air Niugini and I do booking for group travels and this is another experience to get guests out of PNG" ‎ ‎She said more than 20 people from Buka, Port Moresby and Milne Bay have expressed interest in this endeavor.

‎She added that her tour company will be assisting participants with passport processing. ‎ ‎Ms. Joel emphasized that this international tour won't be the last, they have plans to visit Jerusalem on the next international tour.

While low river levels have temporarily halted normal freight transport along parts of the Fly, the company has activated cont
item.content:encoded:
Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML] says operations at its Western Province mine site are continuing safely despite ongoing dry weather lowering water levels along the Fly River.

In a statement, OTML confirmed it is closely monitoring weather impacts on its primary supply route. While low river levels have temporarily halted normal freight transport along parts of the Fly, the company has activated contingency measures to maintain essential supplies.

Alternative logistics routes are currently being utilized to deliver fuel, heavy equipment, consumables, and critical operational materials directly to the mine site.

OTML Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Kedi Ilimbit assured stakeholders that business continuity plans are effectively keeping operations on track.

"As part of our business continuity planning, Ok Tedi has been actively managing the impacts of the dry conditions through alternative supply routes and careful management of key resources," Ilimbit said.

He said alternative supply routes have introduced logistical challenges and driven up operational costs, but core mining and processing activities remain fully operational.

item.title: Hela Provincial Government allocates K12 million in emergency drought relief
item.description: ​In response to the severe El Niño conditions devastating the country, the Hela Provincial Government has stepped in to provide immediate relief supplies, including emergency food rations and clean drinking water, to affected communities across the province. ​Prolonged drought conditions have dried up vital water sources and severely damaged subsistence crops, leaving thousands of people facing ac
item.content:encoded:
​In response to the severe El Niño conditions devastating the country, the Hela Provincial Government has stepped in to provide immediate relief supplies, including emergency food rations and clean drinking water, to affected communities across the province.

​Prolonged drought conditions have dried up vital water sources and severely damaged subsistence crops, leaving thousands of people facing acute food and water shortages.

​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed that the Provincial Executive Council [PEC] has approved a K12 million relief package to address the escalating humanitarian crisis. ​ "The funds will be distributed across all 300 wards in Hela Province, with each ward slated to receive K40,000 for direct relief efforts. K9 million has already been released and is currently being processed to reach ward accounts as quickly as possible," he said.

​Governor Undialu emphasized that while K12 million appears to be a substantial sum, distributing it across 300 wards means the funds will be stretched thin. However, he emphasized that providing immediate, tangible support to families during this disaster remains the government's top priority.

​He has maintained the provincial government’s commitment to reallocating resources to ensure public survival.

​"We are putting every effort and every resource into helping our people. If it means putting a halt to ongoing development projects, such as road construction, we will do so to save lives," Governor Undialu stated.

​He further cautioned that if drought conditions worsen, the provincial government is prepared to bring all non-essential development activities to a complete standstill, redirecting every available kina toward life-saving operations.

Recognizing that provincial resources alone may not be enough for long-term relief, Governor Undialu said the Hela provincial government will engage with the national government, international aid organizations, and donor agencies to secure additional disaster assistance and relief supplies for the province.

item.title: Police minister warns of law and order risks during El Nino
item.description: Police Minister Sir John Pundari has sounded a strong warning as Papua New Guinea braces for what experts say could be the most severe El Nino in the nation’s history. Minister Pundari said that while the government is preparing for widespread drought, water shortages, and other impacts, the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] will play a critical role in maintaining law and order during t
item.content:encoded:
Police Minister Sir John Pundari has sounded a strong warning as Papua New Guinea braces for what experts say could be the most severe El Nino in the nation’s history.

Minister Pundari said that while the government is preparing for widespread drought, water shortages, and other impacts, the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] will play a critical role in maintaining law and order during this period.

“The RPNGC is coordinating with the PNG Defence Force [PNGDF], disaster authorities, and provincial governments to ensure security during the crisis.

“Strict orders have been issued for police to crack down on any exploitation of the El Nino disaster for personal or criminal gain. Anyone who exploits the misery of another human being is a disgrace, and they will face charges for any crimes they commit,” Sir John said.

He has assured the public that police will be on high alert for civil disorder and criminal activity linked to resource scarcity.

With the support from the government, the RPNGC is planning ahead to ensure resources are distributed fairly and communities remain resilient.

The police minister is urging communities to take note of the following impacts of El Nino and prepare in advance: • Severe drought and delayed wet season • Water rationing and intermittent supply • Power shortages in hydro dependent regions • Heat stress driving demand for cooling in cities • Settlement pressures where water is already scarce • Social tensions linked to resource scarcity • Bushfires and vegetation die off • Air quality deterioration from dust and smoke

Police throughout the country have been directed to work closely with community leaders to minimize El Niño-related crimes.

item.title: New MV Karkar to boost travel and cargo movement in Vanimo
item.description: The arrival of the new MV Karkar at Vanimo Wharf is being welcomed as a potential boost to passenger travel and the movement of cargo in West Sepik, particularly at this time when businesses in Vanimo are struggling to maintain supplies. Owned by Lutheran Shipping Services and operated under IROK Shipping Services, the modern vessel is offering another option for the people and businesses that dep
item.content:encoded:
The arrival of the new MV Karkar at Vanimo Wharf is being welcomed as a potential boost to passenger travel and the movement of cargo in West Sepik, particularly at this time when businesses in Vanimo are struggling to maintain supplies.

Owned by Lutheran Shipping Services and operated under IROK Shipping Services, the modern vessel is offering another option for the people and businesses that depend on sea transport to move passengers, goods, and supplies along the coast.

For businesses in Vanimo, reliable shipping is critical. Store owners and traders depend on ships to bring in food, building materials, trade goods, and other essential supplies.

Business houses also move goods from the Batas Trade Centre to markets and communities in Wewak, Madang and Lae.

Vanimo Chamber of Commerce Chairman, Gerald Gubon, says the limited number of shipping services calling in at Vanimo has already affected the supply of goods in local shops.

“MV Karkar will help our business houses here greatly. Because we have only one container ship that comes to Vanimo.

In the last three months, we have only received cargoes once. That is why our shops are running low on supplies, the shelves in the shops are almost empty,” Gubon said.

The new ship will provide businesses with another way to move cargo, including smaller consignments, small vehicles, and other bulky goods.

IROK Services Chief Executive Officer Michael Chan Jnr says MV Karkar is expected to travel to Vanimo once a month, though the ship runs could increase based on customer demand.

He says small businesses will also be able to communicate directly with IROK representatives to arrange their cargo.

“Small businesses can now communicate directly with our officers on the ground. Once they communicate, we can have their cargoes shipped out when the vessels come into port,” Chan said.

For ordinary passengers, the ship has a more modern travel option. At about 40 metres long and capable of carrying up to 317 passengers, MV Karkar is designed to transport both people and cargo, with modern passenger facilities and safety systems that will provide a comfortable journey.

item.title: NBC TV to air Sheilla Yama’s Title-Retaining Bout tonight at 7:30 PM
item.description: The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) will broadcast a replay of Papua New Guinean boxer Sheilla Yama's latest title fight tonight at 7:30 pm on NBC TV. Yama, who hails from Mt Hagen, successfully defended her IBF International super lightweight title over the weekend in Auckland, New Zealand, defeating Australia's Jessica Messina on a unanimous points decision.
item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) will broadcast a replay of Papua New Guinean boxer Sheilla Yama's latest title fight tonight at 7:30 pm on NBC TV.

Yama, who hails from Mt Hagen, successfully defended her IBF International super lightweight title over the weekend in Auckland, New Zealand, defeating Australia's Jessica Messina on a unanimous points decision.

The bout, held at Eventfinda Stadium on Auckland's North Shore, served as the main support fight on the Duco Events Ltd and Parker Promotions card.

The contest went the full ten-round distance for the first time in Yama's professional career, with judges scoring the fight in her favour across all three cards.

The win extends her unbeaten professional record to eight wins from eight fights, with three victories by stoppage.

Ranked No.2 in the world at her weight by the International Boxing Federation, Yama could next set her sights on a bout with either IBF No.1 contender Flora Pili of France or No.3 Hannah Robinson of England, with Ireland's Katie Taylor currently holding the IBF world title.

NBC is proud to bring this outstanding performance by one of Papua New Guinea's finest athletes to audiences nationwide.

Viewers are invited to tune in to NBC TV tonight at 7:30 pm to relive Yama's hard-fought victory.

item.title: Solar power project to be commissioned in Hela
item.description: A Solar Power Project at Yangome Village in Komo Hulia Electorate, Hela province is ready to be commissioned on 16th September 2026. The Yangome solar project in Hulia LLG is delivered by the Hela Provincial Government in partnership with Arafura Energies Ltd.
item.content:encoded:
A Solar Power Project at Yangome Village in Komo Hulia Electorate, Hela province is ready to be commissioned on 16th September 2026.

The Yangome solar project in Hulia LLG is delivered by the Hela Provincial Government in partnership with Arafura Energies Ltd.

It will run alongside two 2Mega Wats (MW) gas turbines already installed at Hides in partnership with ExxonMobil. Together, the 3MW of new generation is expected to end years of darkness for many Hela communities.

Hela governor, Philip Undialu said his people have lived for too long in darkness, without reliable power.

“On September 16th, we will switch on cheaper, reliable and sustainable electricity for Hela. This is our 50th Anniversary gift to our people," Undialu said.

Governor Undialu said the project aligns with the National Government’s broader policy to transfer the management of C-Centres to Provincial Governments and the private sector.

He said the model offers a practical solution to strengthen electricity services and ease pressure on the struggling PNG Power system.

"Through Hela Provincial Government and Arafura Energies Ltd, we are taking control of our energy future. This initiative will ensure our people, businesses, schools and health facilities have access to power that is affordable and dependable," he said.

Hela governor said the power rollout is about more than just lights. He said it will create new economic opportunities, support small businesses, improve service delivery in schools and hospitals, and lay the foundation for future industries in the province.

"For Hela, this is more than a power project. It is about opportunity. Hela will never be the same again," he said.

item.title: Border Command officers challenged to strengthen leadership
item.description: 27 Police officers from across the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary’s Border Command have been challenged to strengthen leadership and supervision within the force after completing a six-week Sergeant Course in Wewak.
